one_line: A patient carrying the early-onset Alzheimer's PSEN1 E280A mutation remained cognitively unimpaired for three decades longer than expected, likely due to a homozygous APOE3 Christchurch mutation that restricted tau pathology despite high amyloid burden.
summary: This case report details a female patient from a large Colombian kindred who carries the PSEN1 E280A mutation, which typically causes early-onset autosomal dominant Alzheimer's disease. Remarkably, she did not develop mild cognitive impairment until her seventies, nearly three decades after the expected onset age. Genetic sequencing revealed that she was homozygous for the rare APOE3 Christchurch (R136S) mutation. Brain imaging demonstrated an unusually high amyloid burden, but notably limited tau tangle pathology and neurodegeneration compared to younger, cognitively unimpaired PSEN1 carriers. Additional in vitro experiments showed that the mutant APOE3ch protein exhibited impaired ability to promote amyloid-beta aggregation. These findings suggest that the APOE3 Christchurch mutation confers strong resistance to tauopathy and clinical Alzheimer's disease despite high amyloid accumulation, pointing to the APOE-heparin interaction as a potential therapeutic target.

key_claims.claim: The APOE3 Christchurch (R136S) homozygous mutation delayed clinical onset of Alzheimer's disease by three decades in a PSEN1 E280A carrier.
key_claims.evidence: Clinical assessment showing the patient did not develop MCI until her seventies despite the expected onset age of early forties; whole exome and genome sequencing identified two copies of the APOE3ch variant.
key_claims.location: Abstract / Clinical assessments / Whole exome sequencing

key_claims.claim: The APOE3ch mutation restricts tau pathology and neurodegeneration despite heavy amyloid plaque burden.
key_claims.evidence: PiB PET imaging revealed unusually high brain amyloid levels, while FTP PET and structural MRI showed limited tau tangles and neurodegenerative measurements compared to younger PSEN1 E280A mutation carriers.

key_claims.claim: The APOE3ch mutant protein reduces Aβ42 aggregation compared to wild-type APOE3.
key_claims.evidence: Thioflavin T fibrillation assays demonstrated a significantly lower rate of Aβ42 aggregation (p < 0.001) in the presence of ApoE3ch, and a split-luciferase complementation assay showed reduced oligomer formation.
key_claims.location: Amyloid aggregation studies / Extended Data Fig. 3
